title: How I Got A Job At Citibank | Ft. Radha Thali
description: Citibank is one of the world's leading banks with the top HNI Clients(High Net Worth Individuals) in their bag. For B-School students who aim to start a career in the field of banking and Finance, Citibank can be a stepping stone for many B-School graduates, moreover provide them with an upper-hand in their careers ahead. Wondering how to crack all steps leading to interning at your dream company and bagging a PPO as well! A student from Goa Institute of Management gives insight on how to go about your preparation and the do's-and-don'ts during the job placements in a B-school.  *This is a promoted feature. Read stories about GIM here - http://bit.ly/2L7We6a  Summary of this video:  Radha Thali is currently pursuing her PGDM in Finance at Goa Institute of Management. Radha did her summer internship at Citibank as a financial analyst and also converted the PPO. She gives us an overview of all the processes involved from the interview process to executing tasks, and preparation of the final internship presentation.  Radha discusses how Goa Institute of Management helped them in preparing for the summer internship and ultimately crack the PPO. Whether it is the teamwork that Goa Institute of Management induces in its students through activities taking place over the year or specific focus given to students interested in a particular domain, Goa Institute of Management helps in providing the best industry exposure to its students through the PGDM programme.  Here are a few key takeaways from Radha's interview that all aspiring Banking and Finance students must keep in mind:  1. Do thorough research about the organization and job profiles before you start interning. 2. Make sure you put forward your strengths and weaknesses during the interview process. 3. Brush up your Excel skills before starting your job or internship.  4. Get an understanding of what your profile entails. 5. Try to put in extra hours for academics and during your internship. 6. Don't hesitate in clearing your doubt about a task from your superiors. 7. Start jotting down pointers for your final presentation as you start interning.  #Citibank #GIM #GoaInstituteOfManagement #PPO   *This is a promoted feature. asr.full_text: Subscribe to our channel and press the bell icon to never miss an update. So I have completed my undergraduate from Aarey Poda College in Mumbai in Commerce. Then I have done my Masters in Commerce also from Aarey Poda College. College, post that I have done a brief internship with Tata Motor Finance in Corporate Lending. And then I am in GIM because I was inclined towards finance and I wanted to take up MBA. In finance. Since graduation and my Masters in itself was not that beneficial for the. Career path that I really wanted, MBA at that point seemed like the decision that needed. Me to push myself ahead in my career. So the biggest criteria for me would be first the. Ranking of the college, second would be the alumni network because it's a normal college. In let's say Mumbai, it wouldn't have that much of a reach and won't have that reputation. That a college has and which is very important when you're doing an MBA from a B-School. So GIM was a choice for me because GIM had completed 25 years. GIM had a very good reputation. In finance, it had a very good alumni network and these things would matter to me 10 years. Down the line a lot more. A brand like Citi coming to GIM is a huge thing and it is a dream company for many,. Which I am sure because it is the leading global bank and getting an opportunity to. Do your summer internship and for me the very first exposure towards corporate before my. Final job, I really wanted to convert Citi. I started reading about Citi, read their annual report to understand what are the services. And how has Citi been doing and what is Citi into. So I started reading about the GD topics that would be relevant or the questions that could. Be asked based on my subjects that I was pursuing. So that required a lot of studying prior and just reading about the company while preparing. For Citi to come to campus or any big company to come on campus. In order to have something that I know about the field, I had taken up a course of FLIP. About banking and finance fundamentals to have an idea about, you know, the NBFC and. BFSL, how does it function. I had also enrolled for a CFA course so I was preparing, I was reading. Whatever I could along with juggling my academics in terms of I could gather whatever knowledge I. Can and these are the things I could speak about. I don't think I'll ever be able to forget that day. That you get your summer internship. I remember the day very clearly. It started off with a. Pre-placement talk that is unusual for the companies that come to campus where they. They explain about the role and how do you go about the structure for the internship. We had three interviews and by the end of, we started from around 30-40 I think and then. We were just 10 of us at the end of it. Me and a friend of mine, we were called out again, the panelists, everybody was there. And they just said that you know, congratulations, you have been offered a summer internship. And there was excitement like you know, okay I did it and there was a lot of happiness. We reached the office around 8 in the morning and the whole swanky office, like you mentioned,. It was huge. We realised when we stepped in there that I don't know how big Citi as a brand is. And we went in and there were around 45-50 people more in the conference room along with. Us. There were four of us who were interns and the rest one were the permanent employees. That were joining with us. Post that we were introduced to our mentors who later on introduced us to the team members and. Briefed us a little about you know okay how where are you from and what the department does and my. Mentor gave me a few things that i could start reading upon before the project was allotted. So the first day was just about getting to explore getting to understand how the culture is what the. Team is and we were introduced to our team so we were just you know very inquisitive about the fact. That where do we fall in the big umbrella that is Citi, where do we fall in it. To begin with my project was about creating a forecasting model for them, a framework that. Could help them forecast their activities. So for Citi I was in the financial planning and analysis. Team, so I was in the support function for Citi. So when the project was given I was very curious. About you know what would be the end product out of it and what were the expectations from the. Project for me while we started working me and my mentor he guided me towards what could be done. What things i needed to read before coming on board with the project and that helped me because. While i was reading about the concepts and the same time interacting with my team members i. Understood okay what was the what was the reason that the project that the framework was being done. For so the scope of the project was very wide when we started off we did not know what would be the. Exactly end result or how much time would it require there was no structure to it so the. Biggest challenge was at the time constraint towards the project there was very limited time. Two months and then you have to complete their presentation schedule at the end of it and by. The time you start full-fledged so the biggest constraint was the time factor in the project so. The final presentation was scheduled two days prior to the end of my internship and it was a. Very nervous day because the presentation was supposed to be done with the senior leadership. And I was I had not even met few of them during my internship so there was a I was completely. Nervous before the presentation my mentor helped me a lot prepare for the same you know what kind. Of questions could be expected and how do you go about it there was we had prepared well so during. The final presentation I presented post which there were questions asked since the framework. That I was creating was a new one. A lot of people were inquisitive about how it would. Fit in and how it would fit in for city as a whole. So there were questions about the. Same. I think two things that would impress them the most is my hard work and my persistence. So there was a lot of hard work required in terms of the number of hours that you put. In, the dedication with which you do what you do. Because it is not something that you. Can just do with the constraint of, okay, I'm going to come in this time, I'm going. To leave it this time you need to really enjoy and be in the work to do that and the second thing i. Think that really helped me was my inquisitiveness the want to learn the want to you know keep. Pushing myself out of my comfort zone to do something that actually would be useful at the. End of it and not just complete those two months and leave so the day started with something like. We had classes in the morning and uh suppose the classes were just done we were leaving we were. Almost leaving from the classes and that's when the mail came up from Citi saying that. You have received a pre-placement offer and I was with my colleagues and you know I was. Shocked, I had goosebumps and my colleagues just peeped into my phone and everybody knew. Suddenly and there were around 60 students around me and everybody knew and there was. Congratulations and there was a happy vibe all around. Post that I called my mom dad. And it was a beautiful experience. So before I start my job with Citi in three months time,. I have taken up courses for Excel for financial modelling which is what I did and I want to. Better myself in it. Also, we had a course for financial modelling in the previous term. So taking it further from that I am preparing on the similar lines of what I did in my internship. And how I could do better.
